assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, roughly half the TW average of 12,000-15,000 km/yr. All checkpoints use assumed_km = 7000 * years (7000 / 21000 / 35000 / 49000 / 70000). Two consequences are baked into every number below. (1) Resale is quoted from LOW-MILEAGE listings, which in the TW RAV4 market sit clearly above the mileage-blind average — visible directly in the fetched 8891 rows: a 2023 2.5 Hybrid 旗艦 at 62,900 km asks 819,000 while the same trim at 119,400 km asks 755,000. (2) Servicing is TIME-driven, not mileage-driven: Toyota TW's interval is 每 6 個月或 10,000 公里，以先到者為準, so at 7,000 km/yr the 6-month clock always fires first and this owner pays for roughly 20 shop visits across 10 years while covering only 70,000 km. That makes per-km maintenance cost look high and makes age-based consumables (tires, 12V battery, brake fluid, coolant) — not wear-based ones — the dominant spend. Tax (牌照稅/燃料稅) and insurance are excluded by design throughout. IMPORTANT on price platforms: all 8891 and SUM figures are 車商售價 (dealer RETAIL asking). Every private_sale_price below is converted DOWN from that level by 11% (factor 0.89) at every checkpoint including year 1, and dealer_tradein_price is a further 13-14.5% below private. An earlier draft of this record used a 7% retail→private spread at year 1, which is outside the realistic 8-15% band; that has been corrected. Note also that the two platforms disagree more than commonly assumed — for 2021 2.5 Hybrid 旗艦 at comparable mileage, 8891 sits roughly 17% below SUM (8891: 88,000 km = 538,000; SUM: 92,558 km = 648,000) — so retention ratios here are blended toward the 8891 (lower) side rather than taken from SUM alone.

purchase.source: List price 1,040,000 INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED in this pass by fetching the TVBS 地球黃金線 2026 RAV4 spec/price table, which returns the full 6th-gen TW hybrid lineup: 豪華 1,040,000 / 尊爵 1,170,000 / 尊爵+ 1,220,000 / 旗艦 1,300,000 / Adventure 4WD 1,330,000 / GR Sport 4WD 1,390,000 / PHEV 4WD 1,490,000. This matches the prior researcher's figure exactly (0% difference), so list_price is unchanged. Discount 25,000 is INFERRED, not observed: no transaction menu for the 豪華 trim specifically could be found. Observed 6th-gen deals span a wide range — WeWanted (fetched) shows a 2026 2.5 Hybrid closing at exactly 1,040,000 (i.e. zero cash discount), 尊爵+ at 1,200,000 vs 1,220,000 list (20,000), GR Sport at 1,340,000 and 1,351,000 vs 1,390,000 list (39,000-50,000), PHEV at full 1,490,000; a PTT 菜單 dated 2026-07-08 (fetched, timestamp decoded from the article id) for the 旗艦 shows 空車折扣 70,000 off a 1,300,000 list. Entry trims discount least on a supply-constrained new generation, so 25,000 (~2.4%) is retained as a mid-conservative figure sitting between the observed 0 and 20,000 entry/near-entry outcomes and the 39,000-70,000 seen on top trims.
purchase.notes: 6th-gen RAV4 is the model year on sale in Taiwan as of 2026-08-11. The 豪華 is the entry hybrid: 2,487cc NA inline-4, 229 hp combined, FWD, e-CVT, 17-inch wheels. There is NO gasoline RAV4 in the 6th-gen TW lineup — the entire range is hybrid or PHEV — and 1,040,000 UNDERCUTS the outgoing 5th-gen hybrid 尊爵 (1,150,000), which matters for resale because it caps what a near-new used example can fetch. Discounts count ONLY genuine dealer cash (空車折扣 + 領牌車折). The 汰舊換新 50,000 and 空汙補助 7,500 on nearly every TW menu are commodity-tax rebates, not dealer money, and are excluded because tax is out of scope; they are also conditional on scrapping an old vehicle. onroad_fees 16,000 = 領牌規費 + 代辦 (~6,000-8,000) + the accessory spend the buyer still carries after gifted items (隔熱紙/踏墊/行車紀錄器, ~8,000-10,000). Menus quote 領牌 25,000-30,000 but that bundle contains first-year 牌照稅 + 燃料稅, excluded here by design; the fetched PTT menu confirms 領牌稅金 is billed separately as 實報實銷, so the tax portion is cleanly separable. real_cost = 1,040,000 - 25,000 + 16,000 = 1,031,000.

selling_costs.notes: Assumes private sale (自售) via 8891 個人刊登, which is what the private_sale_price figures below correspond to. 8,000 sits mid-range for a mainstream C-segment SUV. If the owner trades in at a dealer instead, selling_costs fall to near zero but the realised price drops to dealer_tradein_price — quoting both prices at each checkpoint is what makes that trade-off visible.

value_checkpoints.source: EXTRAPOLATED, but not from nothing — correcting a prior draft that claimed 'no genuine data exists'. 8891 (fetched 2026-08-11) DOES already carry 6th-gen listings: a 2026 Adventure 4WD at 5,499 km asking 1,198,000 against a 1,330,000 list = 90.1% of list at roughly 6 months, dealer retail. Stepping that to 12 months / 7,000 km gives ~87% dealer retail, applied to real_cost = ~897,000 dealer RETAIL asking. private_sale = 897,000 x 0.89 = ~800,000; dealer_tradein = 800,000 x 0.87 = ~695,000. TWO corrections against the prior draft, both downward. (a) It used a 0.93 retail→private factor here, a 7% spread, which is outside the realistic 8-15% band; the standard 0.89 is used instead. (b) Its 1-year proxy read 8891's 2025 model-year listings (935,000 and 949,000) against a 2.0 豪華 list of 1,010,000 to get 93% retention, but 8891's own row labels identify those cars as a 2.0汽油旗艦 (list 1,170,000 → 79.9%) and a 2.5油電曜黑魅影 (list ~1,260,000 → 75.3%). That trim mismatch inflated 1-year retention by roughly 14 points. The 5th-gen 2025 cars are additionally depressed by being an outgoing generation undercut by the new 1,040,000 entry price, so the 6th-gen Adventure data point is the better guide and is what is used. Low-mileage listings quoted throughout.

Predecessor-generation ratio, re-anchored on HYBRID comparables. 8891 (fetched) shows 2023 (3-year) 2.5 Hybrid 旗艦 at 62,900 km asking 819,000 and at 63,100 km asking 819,000, against a 5th-gen Hybrid 旗艦 list of 1,260,000 (KingAutos, fetched) = 65.0% dealer retail; the same trim at 119,400 km asks 755,000 = 59.9%. Interpolating that mileage slope down to our 21,000 km checkpoint, and allowing for a stronger premium at the very low end, gives ~70% dealer-retail retention. 0.70 x real_cost = ~722,000 dealer RETAIL asking. private_sale = 722,000 x 0.89 = ~650,000; dealer_tradein = 650,000 x 0.87 = ~565,000. CORRECTION vs the prior draft (690,000/600,000): it anchored this checkpoint on a 2022 SUM listing described as '旗艦', but the SUM row reads 2.0 旗艦版 — a GASOLINE car — and 8891 shows the powertrains diverge sharply at this age (2023 2.5 Hybrid 旗艦 = 65.0% of list; 2023 2.0汽油旗艦 at 60,000 km = 628,000 = 53.7%; 2023 2.0汽油尊爵 at 60,000 km = 618,000 = 55.7%). Using a hybrid anchor is both more correct and, usefully, confirms the 'Toyota hybrids hold value above market' expectation directly in the data. Quoted from low-mileage listings.

Best age/mileage match in the set. SUM (fetched) lists two 2021 RAV4 2.5 Hybrid 旗艦型 at 38,000 km and 38,012 km, both asking 750,000, plus a 旗艦版 at 44,412 km asking 688,000 and one at 92,558 km asking 648,000. Against a 2021-era Hybrid 旗艦 list of ~1,200,000 (final 5th-gen list is 1,260,000 per KingAutos, fetched; the 2019 launch price for Hybrid FWD 旗艦 was 1,139,000, so a 2021 car sat between) the 38,000 km cars read ~62.5% dealer retail. That is blended DOWN to ~59% because 8891 for the same year and trim runs far below SUM — 8891's 2021 2.5 Hybrid 旗艦 at 88,000 km asks only 538,000 (44.8%) where SUM's 92,558 km car asks 648,000 (54.0%), a ~17% platform gap. 0.59 x real_cost = ~608,000 dealer RETAIL asking. private_sale = 608,000 x 0.89 = ~541,000, rounded to 555,000 to keep a modest low-mileage premium for our 35,000 km checkpoint versus the 38,000 km comparables; dealer_tradein = 555,000 x 0.865 = ~480,000. CORRECTION vs the prior draft (585,000/508,000): it took the comparable's list as '~120萬' and then applied a further +1.5 point low-mileage nudge on top of a car that was ALREADY low-mileage (38,000 km over 5 years = 7,600 km/yr, essentially this buyer's own duty cycle), double-counting the premium. Confidence held at medium: the comparables are 5th-gen 旗艦, not 6th-gen 豪華.

Predecessor-generation ratio, DOWNGRADED to low confidence in this pass. The prior draft rested this checkpoint on a single SUM row — a 2019 Hybrid 4WD 旗艦 at 50,879 km asking 698,000 against a 1,249,000 launch list = 55.9% — which this fact-check could NOT reproduce (the SUM 2016-2019 query returned only 2016/2017 rows, and the 2019-2026 query was not re-fetched). The independent 8891 evidence for 2019 cars sits materially lower: 2019 2.5 Hybrid 旗艦 at 110,000 km asks 580,000 (46.4% of the 1,260,000 list) and 2019 2.0 豪華 at 96,000 km asks 458,000. Retention is therefore shaded from 55.9% to ~54% dealer retail for a low-mileage 49,000 km car. 0.54 x real_cost = ~557,000 dealer RETAIL asking; private_sale = 557,000 x 0.89 = ~496,000, quoted 490,000; dealer_tradein = 490,000 x 0.857 = ~420,000. Cross-check against the trade-in end: 小曾車庫's 收購行情 table (fetched) gives 5代 (2019-2025) a 480,000-1,100,000 band and states explicitly these are 收購的上限值 (acquisition CEILING values) that real offers fall below. Scaling our 420,000 up to the comparable's 1,249,000 purchase cost gives ~509,000, sitting just above their 480,000 floor for the oldest 5th-gen cars — consistent, given ours is a low-mileage example. Confidence low, not medium: the primary anchor is unverified and the two platforms disagree.

EXTRAPOLATED from the PRE-predecessor generation, because the 6th gen is 7 months old and the 5th gen only reaches 7 years, so no 10-year data exists for either. Uses the 4.5-gen (2016 facelift) RAV4 2.5 Hybrid 尊爵, list 1,250,000 at launch, now exactly 10 years old. SUM (fetched and re-verified in this pass): 2016 2.5 Hybrid 2WD at 90,155 km asking 439,000 = 35.1% of list; at 120,000 km asking 488,000 (condition outlier); at 190,533 km asking 368,000. 8891 (fetched) corroborates: 2016 2.5 HYBRID 尊爵 at 133,000 km asking 360,000. Our checkpoint is 70,000 km — well under half the TW norm for a 10-year car — so retention is lifted ~2 points to ~37%. 0.37 x real_cost = ~381,000 dealer RETAIL asking; private_sale = 381,000 x 0.89 = ~339,000, quoted 340,000; dealer_tradein = 340,000 x 0.855 = ~290,000 (a wider dealer margin than at earlier checkpoints, because gross margin on cheap old stock is proportionally larger). Cross-check: scaling our 290,000 to the comparable's 1,250,000 cost gives ~352,000, inside 小曾車庫's 4.5代 290,000-600,000 ceiling band. Low confidence: different generation, different trim, and by year 10 the HV battery is 2 years past its 8年/16萬公里 warranty, which measurably depresses hybrid values in TW even when the pack is healthy. Acknowledged discontinuity: the 7→10 year drop is steeper per year than 5→7, which is unusual for a depreciation curve; it is retained rather than smoothed because it reflects two real effects — the battery-warranty cliff and the switch to a different (weaker) comparable generation.

maintenance.plan_notes: Toyota TW's scheduled interval is 每 6 個月或 10,000 公里，以先到者為準 — at 7,000 km/yr the 6-month TIME trigger always fires first, so this is a TIME-DRIVEN plan: about 2 paid visits a year, roughly 20 visits across 10 years, for only 70,000 km. That is the single most important structural fact in this row. It means (a) per-km maintenance cost is high even though total km are low, and (b) the big-ticket items are AGE-based (tires, 12V battery, brake fluid, coolant) rather than WEAR-based — brake pads in particular last unusually long on a hybrid because regenerative braking does most of the decelerating at this duty cycle. Toyota TW has NO free scheduled-maintenance program; the only freebies are the 滿月免費檢查 and the 半年/1萬公里免費檢查, which is why year 1 is cheap. New-car warranty 3年/10萬公里, HV 電池 8年/16萬公里, HV 馬達 5年/12萬公里 — so HV components are covered through the year-7 checkpoint and exposed only in the 7-10y window. Cost basis is 5th-gen owner receipts recovered from Mobile01 (1萬公里定保 ~2,940元; 3-year T30 定保 at ~35,000 km with tire rotation ~3,400元; 2萬公里保養 6,578元 on a 2.0). CORRECTION applied in this pass: the prior draft put the first (age-out) tire set in the 3-5y window, which made period_cost fall from 35,000 at year 5 to 24,000 at year 7 — a non-monotonic curve. Tires at this mileage age out at roughly 5-6 years, which places the first set in the 5-7y window; moving it there gives a monotonically rising 3,000 / 13,500 / 19,000 / 40,000 / 70,000 and matches the standing guidance of a tire set every 5-6 years. Nothing else was re-costed.

checkpoints.source: Covers 1-3y. Four time-triggered visits at ~2,800元 average (bracketed by Mobile01 receipts: ~2,940元 for a 1萬公里定保, ~3,400元 for the 3-year T30 定保 at 35,000 km including tire rotation), plus brake fluid ~1,500元 and cabin/air filters ~1,600元.

major_items: 4 x 半年定保 (~3,000元 each) — now OUT of the 3年/10萬公里 warranty, so parts are owner-paid
12V 輔助電瓶更換 (auxiliary battery, ~6,000元 — hybrids run a small aux battery, typical TW life 3-5 years)
煞車油更換 (4-year interval, ~1,500元)
煞車來令片 still original — regen braking means almost no pad wear at this duty cycle
輪胎 still in service (original set is ~5 years old at this point; replacement falls in the next window)
checkpoints.source: Covers 3-5y. Scheduled service extrapolated from 5th-gen owner receipts (~3,000元 per time-triggered visit x4 = ~12,000元); 12V aux battery from TW hybrid replacement norms (~6,000元); brake fluid ~1,500元. REVISED DOWN from a prior draft figure of 35,000 by moving the first tire set out of this window — see plan_notes.

major_items: 4 x 半年定保 (~3,200元 each, out of warranty)
第一套輪胎更換 (first tire set, 17吋 — an AGE-out at ~5-6 years, not a tread-out; only ~49,000 km covered by then; ~16,000元 for 4 fitted)
前輪煞車來令片 (first front pad set — deferred to ~year 7 because regenerative braking does most of the deceleration; ~4,500元 fitted)
e-CVT / 混合動力變速機油 (~3,500元, 6-year or 80,000 km item)
煞車油更換 (6-year interval)
雨刷、小型耗材、胎壓感知器電池
HV 電池仍在 8年/16萬公里保固內 — no battery exposure in this window
checkpoints.source: Covers 5-7y. Extrapolated from 5th-gen scheduled-service pricing and TW dealer quote norms for tires, pads and transaxle fluid. REVISED UP from a prior draft figure of 24,000 by moving the age-out tire set into this window, which also restores a monotonically rising maintenance curve. Deliberately excludes German-style out-of-warranty risk items (air suspension, water pump, coil packs) — that guidance targets German cars, and the TW owner-forum record for the 5th-gen RAV4 Hybrid shows no systematic unscheduled failures in this age band.

major_items: 6 x 半年定保 over 3 years (~3,500元 each, ~21,000元)
第二套輪胎 (second tire set, age-out again at ~year 10-11; ~18,000元)
12V 輔助電瓶 第二顆 (~6,500元)
煞車碟盤 + 前後來令片 (discs corrode with age at low mileage more than they wear; ~12,000元)
引擎冷卻液 + 換流器冷卻液 (long-life coolant, 10-year/160,000 km first change, both loops; ~2,500元)
銥合金火星塞 (~4,000元 — 100,000 km rated, so this is an age/precaution change at 70,000 km, deferrable)
煞車油 x2 (8-year and 10-year)
懸吊橡膠襯套／避震器等老化件 provision (~6,000元)

RISK, NOT COSTED: HV 電池保固 (8年/16萬公里) expires during this window. TW replacement quoted at ~62,000元. Excluded from period_cost because 5th-gen TW field data shows failure at 70,000 km is uncommon — but it is the single largest tail risk in this row.
checkpoints.source: Covers 7-10y. Extrapolated. Scheduled-service component follows the same time-driven cadence as earlier windows; consumables priced from TW norms. HV battery replacement cost of ~62,000元 and the 8年/16萬公里 battery / 5年/12萬公里 motor warranty terms come from U-CAR's Toyota hybrid Q&A (search-snippet only; the page body returned HTTP 403). Low confidence: no 6th-gen or even 5th-gen car has reached 10 years, so the whole window is a projection from generic Toyota hybrid age behaviour rather than from receipts.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, roughly half the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000 km/yr. Midpoint 7,000 km/yr used at every checkpoint (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000 km). Taiwan sells exactly one Alphard HEV specification (2.5 HEV 七人座) through 和泰汽車, so this is the exact trim, not a proxy; the 3,300,000 PHEV 六人座 is a separate variant and is NOT priced here. Two consequences drive the record. (1) SERVICING IS TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN: Toyota Taiwan's T30 interval is 每 6 個月或 10,000 公里，以先到者為準 (verified on toyota.com.tw) — at 7,000 km/yr the 6-month clock always fires first, so the owner pays for 2 visits/year and never reaches a mileage trigger. T50 additionally fires on 單數年 and T60 on 雙數年, so those are calendar-driven here too. Tires, brake fluid, coolant and the 12V battery age out before they wear out. (2) RESALE IS ABOVE THE MILEAGE-BLIND AVERAGE: Taiwan Alphards are heavily used for airport transfer / 商務接送, so the public listing pool is dominated by 100,000-200,000 km cars. Every listing found sits far above this buyer's mileage, so each value checkpoint is adjusted UP from observed listings toward the low-mileage end, using a consistent slope (~5 TWD/km at years 1-3 where the observed mileage-price gradient is steep, tapering to ~3 TWD/km by years 5-10 where observed listings show the gradient flattening). Tax (牌照稅/燃料費) and insurance are excluded from every figure by design. All money in TWD.

purchase.source: list_price 3,160,000 independently re-verified for this audit against two sources: Toyota Taiwan's own site (toyota.com.tw/models/alphard/pricing shows the Alphard line as $316.0~330.0萬, where 316萬 = HEV 七人座 and 330萬 = PHEV 六人座), and the 和泰汽車 announcement of 2025-02-06 reported by 2GameSome (HEV 3,160,000, PHEV 3,300,000 added). Both fetched and confirmed 2026-08-11. No later TW price change found. Agrees with the prior researcher's figure to the TWD, so list_price is unchanged. discounts and onroad_fees are reasoned estimates, not quoted figures — see notes.
purchase.notes: DISCOUNT CORRECTED 30,000 -> 0. The prior record set 30,000 on the sole basis of a Mobile01 thread it admitted it could not open (HTTP 403) and had only a search-engine summary of — that is a guess presented as sourced. Independent market evidence points the other way and is verifiable: on 8891 today, one-year-old 2025 HEV cars with 20,000-23,000 km are asking 2,980,000-2,998,000 (94.3-94.9% of the 3,160,000 new list) and a 1,000 km 2025 PHEV asks 3,138,000 against its 3,300,000 list (95.1%). A model whose lightly-used examples change hands at ~95% of list at DEALER RETAIL is not a model carrying a meaningful cash discount on new stock. The Alphard also launched Jun-2023 on a 500-unit annual allocation with waiting lists and no launch promotion. Although Toyota TW generally does discount, this specific model behaves like the allocation-limited Lexus/Porsche cases, so 0 is the correct call. If a dealer confirms a real cash discount, subtract it from real_cost directly. ONROAD FEES (45,000): 新領牌照登記費 + 代辦 (~5,000) plus 配件 appropriate to this class — 隔熱紙 on an MPV with this much glass runs 20,000-30,000 alone, plus 行車紀錄器, 腳踏墊, 鍍膜 (~35,000-40,000 combined). 45,000 is mid-range for a 3.2M luxury MPV, well above the ~15,000 a mainstream sedan needs and below the ~60,000 of a Porsche. EXCLUDED by design: 牌照稅, 燃料費, 強制險與任意險 — none are in real_cost. real_cost = 3,160,000 - 0 + 45,000 = 3,205,000.

value_checkpoints.source: DIRECT current-generation data, INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED for this audit. I fetched auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/alphard myself and confirmed every figure the prior researcher cited, to the TWD: 2025 Hybrid 2.5L 2萬 km -> 2,980,000; 2.3萬 km -> 2,998,000; 5萬 km -> 2,750,000; 7萬 km -> 2,688,000. Also confirmed the near-new anchor: 2025 PHEV 1,000 km -> 3,138,000 against its 3,300,000 list = 95.1% of list at DEALER RETAIL. All of these are 車商售價 (dealer retail asking), not private-sale prices. Applying the 95% near-new ratio to the HEV's 3,160,000 list gives dealer retail ~3,000,000 at this buyer's 7,000 km, consistent with and slightly above the verified 20,000-23,000 km listings, as the low-mileage adjustment requires. ADJUSTMENT MADE: dealer retail 3,000,000 -> private_sale 2,700,000 (-10%, the standard TW 車商售價 vs 自售 spread) -> dealer_tradein 2,380,000 (a further -11.9% for 車商收購). No dealer asking price was copied into private_sale. Confidence high is genuinely earned here: five same-generation listings that I re-fetched and matched exactly, plus an independent near-new ratio anchor. Retention of 84% of real_cost at one year is extreme by general-market standards but correct for this model — TW Alphard/Lexus LM demand and allocation limits are the known outlier case.

DIRECT current-generation data, but thinner than the prior record implied. The 40-series launched in TW Jun-2023, so genuine 3-year-old cars exist only as Jul-Dec 2023 registrations. AUDIT CORRECTION: the prior record excluded '2023 Executive Lounge 2.5L' listings as run-out 30-series cars (TW sold the 30-series as a single Executive Lounge trim until Jun-2023) yet still used a 51,807 km / 2,488,000 datapoint as a clean 40-series anchor. My own 8891 fetch shows that car listed as '2023 Executive Lounge 2.5L, 5.1萬 km, 248.8萬' — i.e. it falls under the researcher's own exclusion rule. The filter was applied inconsistently, keeping the datapoint that suited the answer. Verified 2023 EL 2.5L population on 8891: 5.1萬 km -> 2,488,000; 10萬 km -> 1,990,000; 10萬 km -> 1,770,000; 12萬 km -> 1,770,000. Bracketing evidence I do trust: verified 2025 HEV at 5萬 km -> 2,750,000 and 7萬 km -> 2,688,000, so a 3-year car at 21,000 km must sit below the 1-year figure and above the high-mileage 2023 cars. Estimated dealer retail at 21,000 km ~2,745,000. ADJUSTMENT MADE: dealer retail 2,745,000 -> private_sale 2,470,000 (-10%) -> dealer_tradein 2,160,000 (-12.5%). Raised slightly from the prior record's 2,450,000/2,140,000 to keep the low-mileage uplift consistent with the slope used elsewhere. Confidence medium: bracketed by verified listings on both sides, but clean same-generation same-age datapoints are scarce and one of the two the prior record relied on is of ambiguous generation.

EXTRAPOLATED FROM THE PREDECESSOR GENERATION — the 40-series is only 3 years old in TW and no genuine 5-year-old car exists. Method per instruction: a 2021 car is the 30-series 2.5 Hybrid Executive Lounge, whose official 和泰 list was 2,860,000 (Jun-2021) rising to 2,920,000 (late 2021), verified via the 7Car price history I re-fetched (2018 2,650,000 -> Feb-2020 2,710,000 -> Aug-2020 switch to 2.5 Hybrid 2,840,000 -> Jun-2021 2,860,000 -> late-2021 2,920,000); use 2,880,000. Verified dealer RETAIL asking on 8891 today: 2021 EL 2.5L 6.3萬 km -> 1,888,000 and 9.79萬 km -> 1,880,000, plus SUM 73,811 km -> 2,020,000. AUDIT CORRECTION — THIS IS THE MAIN NUMERIC FIX IN THE RECORD: the prior record adjusted this cohort from a ~78,000 km mean up to 35,000 km by only ~120,000, an implied slope near 1-3 TWD/km, while using 5 TWD/km for the same adjustment at year 3. That inconsistency alone pushed year 5 down and manufactured a depreciation curve that ACCELERATES between years 3 and 5, which no car does and which contradicts the known TW Alphard outlier-retention behaviour. Applying a consistent (and still conservative, because the observed 5-year-old gradient is genuinely flatter) ~3 TWD/km over the 43,000 km gap gives dealer retail ~2,100,000 at 35,000 km. Retention ratio = 2,100,000 / 2,880,000 = 0.73 of the predecessor's original list. Applying 0.73 to this car's real_cost 3,205,000 gives a dealer-retail-equivalent of ~2,340,000. ADJUSTMENT MADE: -> private_sale 2,110,000 (-10%) -> dealer_tradein 1,855,000 (-12%). Corroboration: 小曾車庫, a TW buying dealer, published Jul-2024 收購 (trade-in) guidance of 2,100,000-2,550,000 for 2020-2023 hybrids; the prior record's year-5 trade-in of 1,770,000 sat implausibly far below that band two years on, whereas 1,855,000 is consistent with it. Confidence low: predecessor-generation extrapolation and a large mileage adjustment.

EXTRAPOLATED FROM THE PREDECESSOR GENERATION — no genuine 7-year-old 40-series exists. A 2019 car is the 30-series 3.5 V6 Executive Lounge, official 和泰 list 2,650,000 (Feb-2018 TW launch price, unchanged through 2019, verified via 7Car). AUDIT CORRECTION: the prior record quoted five 2019 asking prices including '185,000 km -> 1,388,000' and '186,495 km -> 1,368,000'. My own 8891 fetch shows those two high-mileage 2019 listings (18萬 km and 18.5萬 km) are published as 電洽 — price NOT disclosed. Those two figures were invented and they fed the cohort mean. I discarded them. Verified 2019 3.5 EL dealer RETAIL asking that actually exists: 8.4萬 km -> 1,558,000 and 11.85萬 km -> 1,429,000, mean ~1,493,500 at ~101,000 km. Adjusted UP to this buyer's 49,000 km at ~3 TWD/km gives ~1,650,000, at 5 TWD/km ~1,754,000; I used ~1,700,000 dealer retail. Retention ratio = 1,700,000 / 2,650,000 = 0.64 of the predecessor's original list. Applying 0.64 to real_cost 3,205,000 gives a dealer-retail-equivalent of ~2,050,000. ADJUSTMENT MADE: -> private_sale 1,830,000 (-11%) -> dealer_tradein 1,590,000 (-13%). Net effect of removing the two fabricated datapoints and reworking the arithmetic was small (prior record had 1,810,000/1,560,000), so the prior year-7 figure was substantially right despite the bad inputs. CAVEAT ON THE RECORD: the 2019 donor data is the 3.5 V6, not a hybrid, because that is what exists at that age in TW. The hybrid is the more sought-after drivetrain locally, so this ratio is more likely conservative than optimistic. Confidence low: predecessor generation plus a cross-powertrain substitution.

EXTRAPOLATED, AND THE WEAKEST POINT IN THIS RECORD. A 2016 Alphard in TW predates 和泰's official import (which began Feb-2018 at 2,650,000), so 2016 cars are 外匯車 parallel imports with no official TW list price — the clean ratio method partially breaks here and I am saying so rather than inventing a list price. Verified dealer RETAIL asking: abc好車網 2016 3.5 Executive Lounge -> 1,898,000 (I re-fetched this listing myself and confirmed the 189.8萬 asking price; the page does not publish mileage, which is one reason confidence is low). 8891 verified nearby anchors: 2019 3.5 EL 8.4萬 km -> 1,558,000 and 11.85萬 km -> 1,429,000. Mileage largely stops setting the price by this age — the verified 2021 cohort shows a 63,000 km car asking 1,888,000 and a 97,900 km car asking 1,880,000, essentially identical — which is why the low-mileage uplift here is modest despite this buyer's exceptional 70,000 km at ten years. Estimated dealer retail for a 10-year car at 70,000 km ~1,500,000-1,650,000. Using 2,650,000 (the earliest official 30-series TW list) as the donor denominator gives a ratio of ~0.53; using a plausible 3,000,000 parallel-import transaction price gives ~0.47. I retained the prior record's 0.49. Applying 0.49 to real_cost 3,205,000 gives a dealer-retail-equivalent of ~1,570,000. ADJUSTMENT MADE: -> private_sale 1,400,000 (-11%) -> dealer_tradein 1,190,000 (-15%). The year-7-to-year-10 slide is intentionally faster than year 5 to 7, reflecting the out-of-warranty discount TW buyers apply once a hybrid MPV's HV battery is a decade old. Confidence low, and at the low end of low.

maintenance.plan_notes: TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN. Toyota Taiwan's published schedule (toyota.com.tw/owner_maintenance.aspx, which I re-fetched and verified for this audit) is: T30 = 每 6 個月或 10,000 公里 (engine oil, oil filter, drain-plug washer, 30+ inspection points); T50 = 單數年或每 40,000 公里自 20,000 公里起 (adds cabin filter, spark plugs, brake fluid, 50+ checks); T60 = 雙數年或每 40,000 公里自 40,000 公里起 (adds air filter, brake fluid, coolant, fuel filter, 60+ checks). At 7,000 km/yr this owner NEVER hits a mileage trigger — every service in all 10 years fires on the calendar: 2 T30 visits per year, 20 over the decade, with a T50 layered on in every odd year and a T60 in every even year. AUDIT CORRECTION: the prior record applied that odd/even rule correctly from year 2 onward but omitted it in year 1 — year 1 is 單數年, so the 12-month visit is a T50, not a bare T30. Year-1 period_cost has been raised from 9,000 to 14,000 accordingly. NO FREE MAINTENANCE PROGRAM: unlike some Lexus / Volvo TW packages, Toyota TW includes no complimentary scheduled servicing; only the 1,000 km first inspection is free. Warranty is 3 years / 100,000 km, so years 1-3 carry no repair risk and years 3+ do. PRICES ARE ASSEMBLED, NOT QUOTED: the Toyota TW page explicitly states package content and pricing must be obtained from a service centre ('請洽 TOYOTA 全台服務廠'), so every period_cost is built bottom-up from published item-level TW ranges (oil filter 300-800, air filter 300-1,000, spark plugs 2,000-3,000, brake fluid 2,000-4,000, one tire 17,000+ for this class per pkcar.vip; labour tiers per drivinginstruct's Toyota table) and then uplifted because the Alphard is 和泰's flagship and is serviced at premium-model labour rates. Treat the totals as well-reasoned estimates, not receipts. All amounts are TWD. HYBRID-SPECIFIC: no cam belt (chain), and regenerative braking stretches front pad life a long way — at 7,000 km/yr the first pad change realistically lands around year 6-7, not year 4. Consumables age out rather than wear out: tires replaced at ~year 5 and ~year 10 on age (they will still have tread), brake fluid every 2 years, 12V AGM auxiliary battery roughly every 5 years. Note the period costs do not rise monotonically — the 5-7y window is cheaper than the 3-5y window because the first age-based tire set lands at year 5. That dip is real, not an error. NOT BUDGETED: HV traction battery replacement. Real-world Toyota HV battery failure at 70,000 km is rare and Toyota TW extends coverage on the traction battery well beyond the standard vehicle warranty — but I could not verify the exact current TW hybrid-battery warranty term within this audit, so this remains an assumption and it is the one that would most change the 10-year figure if wrong.

checkpoints.source: Covers 0-1y. Toyota TW official T30 schedule (toyota.com.tw/owner_maintenance.aspx, re-verified) = 6 months or 10,000 km, whichever first; at 7,000 km/yr the 6-month clock fires, so 2 paid visits in year one. RAISED FROM THE PRIOR RECORD'S 9,000: the prior record costed both visits as plain T30s, but Toyota TW's T50 fires 單數年 and year 1 is an odd year, so the 12-month visit is a T50 (adds cabin filter and brake fluid over the T30). Build-up: T30 ~4,500 (0W-16 low-viscosity synthetic ~4.2L, filter, flagship-model labour — above the 500-1,000 oil + 100-200 filter item ranges published by drivinginstruct/pkcar because those are small-car figures) + T50 ~8,500 + ~1,000 consumables = 14,000. Confidence medium: the interval and the odd/even rule are officially sourced, the TWD amounts are assembled from item ranges since 和泰 publishes no package price.

major_items: T30 × 4（每 6 個月，全部由時間觸發而非里程）
第 2 年 T60（雙數年）：空氣濾清器、水箱精、煞車油
第 3 年 T50（單數年）：冷氣濾網、火星塞檢查、煞車油
四輪定位與輪胎調位
仍在 3 年／100,000 km 保固內，不編列故障維修
checkpoints.source: Covers 1-3y (not cumulative). Reviewed and retained from the prior record — the odd/even calendar logic is correct here. 4 × T30 at ~4,000 = 16,000, plus the year-2 T60 (~9,000: air filter, coolant, brake fluid, 60+ point inspection) and the year-3 T50 items (~4,000 incremental: cabin filter, brake fluid) less overlap with the base T30s already counted. Item prices from pkcar.vip's Toyota TW ranges (brake fluid 2,000-4,000, air filter 300-1,000) uplifted for flagship labour. At 21,000 km the 20,000/40,000 km mileage triggers are never the binding constraint, so the calendar rule governs throughout. Nothing breaks in this window — full factory warranty. Confidence medium.

major_items: T30 × 4，含第 4 年 T60 與第 5 年 T50
第一套輪胎更換（約第 5 年，橡膠老化到期而非磨耗到底 — 35,000 km 胎紋還很深）
火星塞（銥合金 4 支）
12V AGM 輔助電瓶第一次更換
水箱精、煞車油
第 3 年原廠保固到期 — 之後所有故障自費
checkpoints.source: Covers 3-5y. Reviewed and retained from the prior record; the build-up is sound. Dominated by ONE item: the first tire set. At 7,000 km/yr the tires reach ~35,000 km with plenty of tread but are 5 years old, and TW shops will not warrant 5-year-old rubber on a 2.2-tonne MPV — so this is an AGE replacement, not a wear replacement. pkcar.vip quotes 17,000+ per tire for this class as an original-fitment figure; a realistic aftermarket premium tire at ~8,500 fitted × 4 + alignment ~36,000. Remainder: 4 × T30 (16,000), iridium spark plugs (~7,000), coolant (~4,000), brake fluid (~3,000), 12V AGM auxiliary battery (~7,000 — hybrids use a small AGM, not a cheap flooded battery). Total ~73,000, rounded to 72,000. The 3-year warranty expires inside this window, which is why it is the first period carrying own-risk. Confidence medium.

major_items: T30 × 4，含第 6 年 T60 與第 7 年 T50
前煞車來令片首次更換 + 碟盤研磨（回充煞車大幅延長壽命，所以拖到第 6-7 年才換）
煞車油、冷氣濾網、空氣濾清器
引擎與 inverter 冷卻液更換
冷氣系統保養、電瓶健檢
襯套／燈泡／雨刷等老化零件
已無原廠保固：計列非排程小修預備金
checkpoints.source: Covers 5-7y. RAISED FROM THE PRIOR RECORD'S 48,000. The prior build-up (4 × T30 16,000 + first front pads and disc skim 12,000 + brake fluid 3,000 + cabin/air filters 5,000 + engine & inverter coolant 5,000 + A/C service and battery check 4,000 + assorted age items 3,000 = 48,000) counted all four visits as bare T30s, but this window contains a year-6 T60 and a year-7 T50 on the calendar rule, and it is the first window entirely outside the 3y/100,000 km warranty on a mechanically complex flagship (twin power sliding doors, rear climate unit, e-mirrors). Added ~8,000 covering the T50/T60 uplift over bare T30s plus a modest unscheduled-repair allowance, giving 56,000. The window is still cheaper than the 3-5y window because no tire set falls here — that is a genuine consequence of age-based tire timing, not an arithmetic slip. First front pad change genuinely deferred this long because the hybrid's regenerative braking does most of the deceleration; a non-hybrid MPV would have needed pads twice by now. Confidence low: no receipts exist for a 40-series Alphard at this age anywhere (the generation is only 3 years old), so this is a reasoned build-up from item prices and hybrid wear behaviour.

major_items: 第二套輪胎（約第 10 年，同樣是老化到期）
12V AGM 輔助電瓶第二次更換
火星塞第二次（時間到期，非里程）
煞車油 × 2、後來令片 + 前碟盤更換
引擎／inverter 冷卻液
電動滑門馬達與滾輪（Alphard 已知的耗損項目）
避震器、懸吊襯套等老化件
冷氣鼓風機／壓縮機保養
未編列：HV 動力電池更換（見 plan_notes 的假設）
checkpoints.source: Covers 7-10y, a 3-year window so naturally the largest. Reviewed and retained from the prior record. Build-up: 6 × T30 (24,000) + second tire set on age (38,000) + 12V AGM battery (7,000) + spark plugs on the calendar rather than mileage (7,000) + brake fluid × 2 (6,000) + rear pads and front discs (14,000) + power sliding-door motor/roller work, a well-known Alphard wear point (12,000) + suspension bushings, A/C and misc age items (11,000) = ~125,000. That is ~42,000/yr, or ~29,000/yr excluding the tire set — high for a Toyota but appropriate for a decade-old 3.2M flagship MPV entirely out of warranty. THE BIG ASSUMPTION, UNCHANGED AND STILL UNVERIFIED: no HV traction battery replacement is budgeted. At 70,000 km a Toyota hybrid battery is very unlikely to have failed, and Toyota TW's extended hybrid-battery coverage should still apply for much of this window — but I could not verify the exact current TW warranty term, so if that assumption is wrong this figure could rise by 150,000-250,000. Confidence low.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/yr, well under the TW average of 12,000-15,000 km/yr. All checkpoints use assumed_km = 7000 * years (7000 / 21000 / 35000 / 49000 / 70000). Two consequences. (1) Resale: at every age this car carries roughly HALF the odometer of a typical TW listing, so every value_checkpoint is benchmarked against the LOW-MILEAGE end of the observed 8891 band, never the mileage-blind average. (2) Maintenance: Lexus TW's published schedule is 6 months / 10,000 km, then 12 months / 20,000 km, 24 months / 40,000 km, 48 months / 80,000 km — whichever comes first. At 7,000 km/yr the TIME trigger always fires first, so the owner pays for 2 visits a year (20 visits over 10 years) while covering only 70,000 km. Keeping every one of those visits on time is also the precondition for Lexus TW's free 5th-year warranty extension, so it is not optional spend. Tax (牌照稅/燃料稅) and insurance are excluded by design throughout. THIS PASS: the whole value_checkpoints block was rebuilt after a cross-vehicle review found the curve sitting below Toyota RAV4 Hybrid at every age and 10 points under the sibling NX 350h at 5 years. The cause was a denominator/repricing error, not a data error — the 8891 evidence itself was re-fetched and held up. Maintenance was not challenged by the review and is carried forward unchanged.

Trim identification: ES / 300h 豪華版 (Luxury) — exact trim confirmed. Base ES300h of the 8th-gen ES, launched in Taiwan 2026-04-28 at 1,770,000. NAMING TRAP, re-verified in this re-audit: the OUTGOING 7th-gen lineup also contained a 1,770,000 car — but that was the ES 200 豪華版 (gasoline), while its ES 300h 豪華版 was 2,030,000 (KingAutos spec page for the 2024 ES 300h 豪華版 shows 定價 203 萬元, opened and read in this pass). value_checkpoints.source: EXTRAPOLATED — the 8th-gen ES has been on sale in Taiwan only since 2026-04-28, so no 1-year-old current-gen car exists. CORRECTED UPWARD IN THIS PASS from 1,260,000/1,110,000. Best evidence is a genuine 8th-gen data point re-confirmed on 8891 (snapshot 2026-08-11): a 2026 MY ES 300h 頂級版 asking 1,783,000 with 33 km — a near-new dealer flip at 90.5% of its 1,970,000 list at roughly 0.2 years. Decaying that to 1.0 year on a model that launched with 1,000+ pre-orders and a delivery queue (a 1-year-old car is available NOW, which supports price) gives ~88% dealer retail ask; 0.88 x real_cost 1,705,000 = ~1,500,000. Sibling cross-check: the NX 350h and RX 350h records both imply ~90% dealer-retail retention at one year, so 88% for a sedan is deliberately conservative against its own showroom. SECOND anchor, now treated as a floor rather than the primary: 7th-gen 300h 豪華版 on 8891 at ~1.4 years — 1,588,000 @ 20,000 km (桃園), 1,558,000 @ 25,000 km and 1,558,000 @ 25,800 km (高雄, both re-fetched today) — which is 76.8-78.2% of that car's 2,030,000 list; see the year-3 note for why that denominator now understates. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: dealer retail ask x 0.885 = private sale (1,330,000), then x 0.875 = dealer trade-in (1,165,000). These are the same haircuts the NX 350h record uses, replacing the slightly heavier ad-hoc haircuts used here before. Every 8891 figure quoted is 車商售價, never what the owner receives.

EXTRAPOLATED from the 7th-gen ES300h 豪華版 at the same age. CORRECTED UPWARD IN THIS PASS from 1,015,000/890,000 — this is the checkpoint where the reviewer's denominator objection bites hardest, and it is upheld. THE ERROR: the prior draft took today's 8891 asks for 7th-gen ES300h 豪華版 cars, divided them by that car's 2,030,000 list, and applied the resulting ratio to our 1,705,000 real_cost. But those asks are August-2026 asks, i.e. already marked down because a brand-new, better-equipped 8th-gen ES 300h 豪華版 now costs 1,770,000 — a 260,000 (12.8%) cut to the same nameplate. Dividing a post-cut used price by the pre-cut 2,030,000 list charges that price cut to the car twice: once in the numerator, where the market has already repriced it, and again when the depressed ratio is multiplied onto the already-lower 1,705,000 base. That is exactly the systematic under-statement the review describes, and it is why the whole curve sat under a RAV4. RE-FETCHED EVIDENCE (8891, snapshot 2026-08-11): 2023 MY 300h 豪華版 1,318,000 @ 30,000 km (台中) and 1,350,000 @ 57,500 km (台北) — note the higher-mileage car asks MORE, so mileage is not driving this small sample. Centre ~1,334,000. Raw ratio to the 2,030,000 list = 65.7%; ratio to the current 1,770,000 replacement price = 75.4%. Neither is right on its own: 65.7% double-counts the cut, and 75.4% assumes outgoing-generation dealer stock has been fully and instantly repriced, which it plainly has not. INDEPENDENT THIRD ANCHOR, new in this pass, which resolves the ambiguity: the ES 200 豪華版 — a Lexus ES sedan that actually listed at 1,770,000, our car's exact price point. Its 8891 asks (re-fetched today, all 實體車行) are 2023 MY 1,008,000 @ 60,000 km, 2022 MY 1,098,000 @ 33,000 km, 2022 MY 1,008,000 @ 60,000 km. Mileage-correcting the 3-year point to our 21,000 km gives ~1,160,000 for a gasoline ES 200, and the same dataset shows the hybrid carries a 6-16% absolute premium over the gasoline car at matched age and mileage (e.g. at 4 years: 300h 豪華版 1,278,000 @ 27,000 km vs 200 豪華版 1,098,000 @ 33,000 km). That lands an 8th-gen ES300h at 3 years / 21,000 km at ~1,250,000-1,280,000 dealer ask, i.e. ~74% of real_cost. SETTLED AT 74% dealer retail = ~1,262,000. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: x 0.885 ask-to-private (1,115,000), then x 0.875 private-to-trade-in (975,000). Result is 65.4% of real_cost, which now sits between the RAV4 Hybrid (63.0%) and the NX 350h (69.3%) as the cross-vehicle review expects, with the sedan-versus-SUV gap preserved rather than erased.

EXTRAPOLATED and INTERPOLATED — no current-gen data exists. CORRECTED UPWARD IN THIS PASS from 890,000/775,000, applying the same de-contamination described at year 3. VERIFIED 7th-gen 豪華版 brackets on 8891 (snapshot 2026-08-11): 2022 MY (4 yr) 1,278,000 @ 27,000 km (台中) and 1,288,000 @ 39,000 km (桃園); 2020 MY (6 yr) 1,012,000 @ 57,000 km (高雄) and 828,000 @ 70,000 km (新北). Straight 4yr-to-6yr interpolation gives ~1,145,000 at 5 years and ~42,000 km; our car is at 35,000 km, at the low-mileage end of that band, so ~1,180,000 in absolute money. Expressed against the outgoing car's own list (2,030,000 facelift / ~1,890,000 pre-facelift, blended ~1,960,000) that is 60.2% — the contaminated figure the prior draft used. Expressed against the 1,770,000 current replacement price it is 66.7%. INDEPENDENT ES 200 CONSTRUCTION, the tiebreaker: the ES 200 豪華版, which genuinely listed at 1,770,000 (facelift) / 1,730,000 (pre-facelift), shows 2022 MY (4 yr) 1,098,000 @ 33,000 km = 62.0% and 2020 MY (6 yr) 958,000 @ 55,000 km = 55.4%, interpolating to ~58.7% at 5 years and ~44,000 km, or ~60% at our 35,000 km. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: x 0.885 ask-to-private (975,000), then x 0.875 private-to-trade-in (855,000). Result is 57.2% of real_cost — inside the 55-60% band the review asked for, and between the RAV4 Hybrid (53.8%) and the NX 350h (62.3%). Confidence stays LOW: this is an interpolation between two extrapolations, one of the two denominators (~1,890,000 pre-facelift) could not be verified, and year 5 is exactly where the free warranty extension expires, which usually puts a step in the curve that a smooth interpolation does not capture.

Rebuilt instead by interpolating the two rows that ARE live at low mileage — 6 yr @ 57,000 km = 1,012,000 and 8 yr @ 69,500 km = 818,000 — to ~915,000 at 7 years, then nudged to ~940,000 because our car is at 49,000 km, below both comparables. Against the ~1,890,000 pre-facelift list that is 49.7%; against the 1,770,000 current replacement it is 53.1%. Caveat kept honest: this year's 8891 spread is noisy (the 140,000 km 2019 car asks more than a 70,000 km 2020 car), the ~1,890,000 denominator could not be verified — KingAutos's partial pre-facelift trim list does not even show a 300h 豪華版 — and no 7-year data can exist for this generation. EXTRAPOLATED ACROSS TWO GENERATIONS — still the weakest point in this record. Nudged up in this pass from 520,000/440,000 for curve consistency, not because new evidence appeared. THE ANCHOR WAS RE-VERIFIED THIS PASS on the 2015-2018 filtered 8891 page (snapshot 2026-08-11): 2016 MY 6th-gen ES300h 豪華版, 570,000, 77,000 km, 台北市 — mileage 7.7k/yr, almost exactly this buyer's profile — and it is confirmed 個人自售 (private individual), the ONLY private listing on that page, every other row carrying the 實體車行 dealer badge. It is therefore already a PRIVATE ask and needs no dealer-to-private haircut; the pre-audit draft that applied one was double-discounting. KEY SIMPLIFICATION available here that is not available at the younger checkpoints: the 6th-gen ES300h 豪華版 listed at ~1,790,000 and our car lists at 1,770,000, so this is very nearly a like-for-like transfer in absolute money rather than a ratio applied across different price points — which is also why the new-generation price cut barely distorts this checkpoint. Build: 570,000 private ask, less ~5% for private ask-to-transaction negotiation, plus ~5% credit for our 70,000 km against its 77,000 km and for the newer TNGA-K platform ageing better; the two net out, so private_sale_price = 570,000 (33.4% of real_cost). Dealer trade-in at x 0.855 = 490,000. Cross-check from the dealer side, also re-verified today: 2016 MY 旗艦版 (the TOP trim) asks 628,000 @ 60,000 km and 628,000 @ 62,000 km from dealers in 新北市, implying roughly a 550,000-580,000 dealer ask for a base 豪華版 at 70,000 km, which lands private in the 490,000-570,000 zone. Confidence LOW: two generation jumps, a single private anchor, and the 6th-gen 豪華版 list of 1,790,000 is the one denominator this record still cannot independently verify — U-CAR was re-tried in this pass and still returns HTTP 403.

maintenance.plan_notes: TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN. Lexus Taiwan's published plan (VERIFIED at lexus.com.tw/service/maintenance-plan.aspx) is: free inspection in the first month after registration, then 6 months / 10,000 km, 12 months / 20,000 km, 24 months / 40,000 km, 48 months / 80,000 km — whichever comes first. At 7,000 km/yr this buyer NEVER reaches a km trigger, so the 6-month clock always fires: 2 visits a year, 20 visits over 10 years, covering only 70,000 km. NO FREE SCHEDULED MAINTENANCE PROGRAM beyond that first-month inspection; everything after is paid. What Lexus TW does give is warranty, verified at lexus.com.tw/service/warranty.aspx: 4 years / 120,000 km basic, extended FREE to a 5th year / 140,000 km if the owner services every six months without delay — one missed appointment forfeits it — plus 3 years unlimited-mileage on the 12V battery (free replacement inside 2 years, 50% contribution in year 3) and 3 years on tyres for manufacturing defects. That is why years 1, 3 and 5 carry no repair contingency and year 7 is where out-of-pocket risk begins. It also means the 20 visits are not discretionary: skipping any of them costs the 5th year of warranty. Cross-check (VERIFIED): 自由時報汽車 reports ES200/ES250/ES300h scheduled maintenance all totalling ~NT$30,000 to 60,000 km — but that is 6 mileage-driven services. Our buyer needs ~8.5 years and ~17 time-driven visits to cover the same 60,000 km, which is exactly why the totals here are higher: lower cost per visit, far more visits. Per-visit basis used: 6-month routine (0W-20 oil + filter + inspection) ~3,200; 12-month annual (adds engine air and cabin filters) ~5,800; 24-month (adds brake fluid) ~9,500; 48-month major (adds transmission fluid, spark plugs, coolant service) ~16,000. These per-visit prices are TW market estimates, NOT sourced receipts. Hybrid-specific: no timing belt, no clutch, and regenerative braking makes pads last far past this mileage — but brake DISCS rust-pit from light short-trip use, and the 12V AGM auxiliary battery is the single most common failure on a low-mileage Lexus hybrid because short trips never fully recharge it. HV traction battery coverage (8 years / 160,000 km) means no pack replacement is budgeted in this 10-year / 70,000 km window. NOT CHALLENGED by the cross-vehicle review and carried forward unchanged in this pass; no independent evidence was found against it.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year; midpoint 7,000 km/year used at every checkpoint (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000 km), roughly half the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000 km/year. At 7,000 km/year the 6-month clock always fires first, so servicing is fully TIME-driven — 2 visits a year, 20 over 10 years, regardless of how little the car is driven. Low mileage does NOT cut the visit count for this brand; it only keeps each visit on the lighter side of the price book and defers high-mileage milestone items. Drivetrain (FWD vs E-Four AWD) for this specific trim could NOT be confirmed on any reachable source — lexus.com.tw/showroom/NX does not break out per-trim specs and the Yahoo 汽車 trim page omits 驅動方式 — so no drivetrain claim is made. Listing fees on 8891/FindCar are modest. On a dealer trade-in these costs largely disappear because the dealer absorbs reconditioning, which is part of why dealer_tradein_price is lower. Dealer retail centred at NT$1,560,000. Chain: private = retail x 0.885 = NT$1,380,000; trade-in = private x 0.875 = NT$1,205,000. Downgraded from 'high' to 'medium': four real listings exist, but they span a 30% range for the same model year, which is not a high-confidence evidence base.

maintenance.plan_notes: TIME-DRIVEN, and that is the single most important fact for this buyer. The interval 每半年或每行駛1萬公里，以先到者為準 was independently confirmed on the 風傳媒 breakdown of Lexus Taiwan's official cost table. At 7,000 km/year the 6-month clock always wins, so the owner makes 2 shop visits per year — 20 over 10 years — even though the car covers only 70,000 km total. Low mileage does not cut the visit count; it only keeps each visit lighter and pushes expensive mileage milestones (spark plugs, coolant, transaxle fluid at ~100,000 km) past the 10-year mark, where the TIME criterion catches them instead. NO FREE SCHEDULED MAINTENANCE — verified directly on lexus.com.tw/owners-warranty.aspx, which describes warranty and service options but bundles no complimentary servicing. What Lexus TW offers instead is the 新車準時保養愛車享延長保證方案 (lexus.com.tw news article dated 2023-12-29, effective Jan 2024): 8 consecutive on-time 定保 using factory packages earns a free warranty extension of 1 year or 20,000 km, transferable with the car; owners who miss a service can instead buy cover for ~NT$25,900. So period_cost below is real out-of-pocket spend, unreduced. Warranty backdrop, all verified on the official page: new car 4 years / 120,000 km; HV battery 5yr/100,000km factory + 3yr/60,000km from the distributor = 8 years / 160,000 km; self-paid genuine parts 2 years / 50,000 km. Cost calibration: 風傳媒's reproduction of the official 定保 table gives a full-cycle-to-100,000 km total in the NT$53,670-64,350 band depending on variant, so the NT$58,350 figure used for the 350h 豪華版 (~NT$5,835/visit over 10 visits) is consistent with the published range; the itemised per-milestone official table could NOT be retrieved (U-CAR and the Bahamut work-order thread both 403), which is why maintenance confidence is capped at medium even in the early years. Owner receipts corroborate the per-visit level but are proxies, not exact matches: the PTT work-order post is an NX200 GASOLINE car, not a 350h — its owner runs the same 7,000 km/year, 6-month cadence and paid ~NT$3,300 for the first 半年保 and just over NT$7,000 for the 10,000 km service after declining the cleaning package; Mobile01 owners report NT$4,000-7,000 for a fuller annual service (that thread is not directly fetchable, so it is treated as weak corroboration only). Consumables here are AGE-driven, not wear-driven — tyres are replaced because the rubber has aged in Taiwan's humidity (~every 5-6 years), never because tread is gone at 35,000 km, and hybrid regenerative braking means pads last far longer than on a conventional SUV. Not budgeted but flagged: an HV battery failure after year 8 (out of warranty) would run roughly NT$150,000-250,000; at 70,000 km on a Lexus that is a low-probability tail, so it is stated rather than folded into period_cost.

major_items: 2 x time-driven 定保 at 6 and 12 months (6-month clock fires first at 7,000 km/yr)
Engine oil + oil filter + drain plug gasket x2
Multi-point inspection, fluid top-up, tyre rotation
Free 1,000 km new-car check (和泰)
Wiper blades
Everything else covered by the 4-year / 120,000 km new-car warranty
checkpoints.source: Official Lexus TW 定保 table as reproduced by 風傳媒 (full cycle to 100,000 km in the NT$53,670-64,350 band; ~NT$5,835/visit for this variant), cross-checked against a verified PTT work order — first 半年保 ~NT$3,300, 10,000 km service just over NT$7,000 — and Mobile01 owner reports of NT$4,000-7,000 for a fuller annual service. Year 1 is the cheapest year: the 6-month visit is nearly empty on a new car (~NT$3,000) and the 12-month visit is a time-based oil service rather than the fuller 10,000 km milestone, since the car has covered only 7,000 km (~NT$6,000). assumptions.notes: Low-mileage owner: 6,000-8,000 km/yr vs the Taiwan average of ~12,000-15,000 km/yr. All checkpoints use assumed_km = 7000 * years. This cuts two different ways. (1) Servicing: the Lexus TW official 保養計劃 sets the interval at 6 months / 10,000 km, so at ~7,000 km/yr the schedule is entirely TIME-driven — two dealer visits every year, roughly 3,500 km apart, never a mileage-triggered one. Low mileage therefore does NOT halve the service count; it only makes each visit cheaper. (2) Resale: 7,000 km/yr puts the car well below the mileage a Taiwanese used-car buyer expects at a given age. MATERIAL CORRECTION APPLIED IN THIS REVISION: the previous version of this record misread 8891's mileage badges by a factor of ten — it recorded the 2024 RX350 旗艦版 as '3,120 km' and the 2023 RX350 頂級版 as '4,200 km', when the site prints 3.12萬公里 (31,200 km) and 4.2萬公里 (42,000 km). Both were re-fetched on 2026-08-11 and the 萬 reading is confirmed (the same page's 2.2萬公里 and 11.9萬公里 badges were recorded correctly as 22,000 and 119,000 km, so the unit convention is not in doubt). Consequence: the year-1 and year-3 anchors are NORMAL-to-high mileage cars (14,000-15,600 km/yr), not near-delivery ones. That means the low-mileage premium this profile earns at those points is real and was previously ASSUMED AWAY, not double-counted — the opposite of the year-5/year-10 error. It is credited here, but capped by the trim-price ceiling (see the 3-year note). Tax (牌照稅/燃料稅) and insurance are excluded from every number by design. Engine is 2393cc, sitting just under the 2,400cc line, i.e. the 1,801-2,400cc 牌照稅 bracket (~11,230/yr) — the same bracket as the 1,998cc predecessor RX200t/RX300 used for the long-horizon extrapolation, so no tax-bracket distortion contaminates the retention transfer. Note this is NOT true of the RX350h (2487cc), which sits one bracket up; that difference is discussed in the checkpoint sources as one of the two forces holding the gasoline/hybrid resale gap small.

purchase.source: UNCHANGED IN THIS REVISION — the reviewer did not object to the purchase block and no new evidence contradicts it. List price INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED on 2026-08-11 against two sources: (a) Lexus Taiwan official site, which shows the RX range at NT$246~361萬 for powertrains 500h/450h/350h/350; (b) the TVBS 地球黃金線 2026 Lexus RX spec table, which resolves that range by trim — 350豪華版 NT$2,460,000 / 2393cc, 350h豪華版 2,560,000 / 2487cc, 350頂級版 2,680,000, 350h頂級版 2,780,000, 350 F Sport 2,950,000, 350旗艦版 2,950,000, 350h旗艦版 3,050,000, 450h+豪華版 3,150,000, 450h+旗艦版 3,550,000, 500h F Sport Performance 3,610,000. All listed as 2026 model year. 2,460,000 is confirmed exactly. Discount: PTT 車板 購車菜單 for the gasoline RX350. The Nov-2025 豪華版 menu was fetched and verified real: 246萬 list, 29萬 off, 217萬 final, with 隔熱紙/行車記錄器/鑰匙皮套/滿油 as free 贈品 and 保險/領牌 billed 實報實銷 (so 217萬 is the car alone). Additional menus: 豪華版 Jan-2025 total 228萬 (≈18萬 off), 頂級版 Oct-2025 268-30=238萬, 頂級版 26年式 Jan-2026 268-31=237萬 (≈11.6% off). onroad_fees rebuilt bottom-up from the 頂級版 menu's 領牌代辦 and 自費配件 lines with the insurance/tax portion stripped out.
purchase.notes:
Trim identification: RX350 / 豪華版 (Luxury) — 2.4L turbo gasoline (T24A-FTS, 2393cc), AWD. Entry trim of the RX range; the hybrid equivalent is badged RX350h (2487cc) and is a different car.
Arithmetic re-verified: 2,460,000 - 250,000 + 35,000 = 2,245,000. The brief's default heuristic ('Lexus barely discounts — use 0') was deliberately NOT applied, because it is contradicted by directly verified transactions. Lexus TW is not a zero-discount brand on the GASOLINE RX: the 汽油 RX350 sells well behind the 350h hybrid locally and dealers clear it with cash. Observed real transactions run 18萬-31萬 off, clustering at 24萬-31萬 (≈10-12%) through late 2025 / early 2026. 250,000 (10.2%) is the central estimate for a normal mid-model-year purchase in Aug 2026 — above the thin Jan-2025 deal, below the Nov-2025 model-year-clearance case, and slightly conservative against the two most recent menus which both ran ~11.6-11.8%. IMPORTANT DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE, now made explicit: because a new 豪華版 transacts at roughly 2,210,000 on the street rather than the 2,460,000 list, every used RX350 competes against a heavily discounted new car. That is a structural drag on this model's retention measured against list, and it is one of the reasons the gasoline RX350 sits slightly below the RX350h at every checkpoint (see the value_checkpoint sources). onroad_fees = 35,000 built as 領牌規費 ~1,500 (新領牌照登記費 + 號牌費) + 經銷商代辦服務費 ~8,000 + 自費配件 ~25,000. The 配件 figure comes from real menus: 鍍膜 12,000 + 電子後視鏡 8,300 in one; FSK 冰鑽隔熱紙升級 + 全車膜 + 天窗 21,500 + 迎賓燈 3,000 in another. The commonly quoted 「領牌費 31,000」 line on Taiwanese 菜單 BUNDLES 強制險 and 汽燃費 into it — those are insurance and tax, excluded here by design, which is why this figure is lower than the raw menu line. Basic 隔熱紙, E-Tag, 防水踏墊, 行車記錄器, 鑰匙皮套 and a full tank are standard 贈品 on Lexus RX menus and are correctly valued at zero.

selling_costs.notes: Unchanged — not objected to and no new evidence against it. Items sum to 14,000 and sit in the upper-middle of the 4,000-15,000 band, which is right for this class. Priced for a private sale (自售) of a large luxury SUV, which is the disposal route private_sale_price assumes. The 過戶 regulatory fee itself is trivial (a few hundred NT$); the 2,500 covers a 代辦 handling 監理站 paperwork. 售前整備 is the big line and scales with class — a 246萬 Lexus SUV needs proper 內裝清潔 + 車身美容 + 輪圈整理 to hold the asking price, so 9,000 rather than the 3,000-4,000 a compact car would need. 刊登費 covers a paid listing slot on 8891/abc好車網 for the weeks a private sale typically takes. If the owner instead trades in to a dealer (dealer_tradein_price), most of this cost disappears — the dealer absorbs 整備 and handles 過戶 — so treat 14,000 as the private-sale path only.

value_checkpoints.source: REVISED (was 1,800,000 / 1,580,000) — a small evidence-driven trim, not a rewrite. Two corrections drove it. (1) MILEAGE UNIT ERROR FIXED: the 8891 comparables are NOT near-delivery cars. Re-fetched 2026-08-11: 2024 RX350 旗艦版 is 3.12萬公里 = 31,200 km asking 2,198,000 (dealer 東威, 認證車), and the 2023 RX350 頂級版 is 4.2萬公里 = 42,000 km asking 1,898,000 — the previous version recorded these as 3,120 km and 4,200 km. (2) The abc好車網 2025 RX 350 旗艦版 at 2,480,000 (dealer 上達汽車) was re-fetched and CONFIRMED to publish no mileage at all, so it cannot carry the weight the previous version put on it. NEW ANCHOR FOUND that constrains the early curve directly: SUM 汽車網 lists a 2024 RX350, 2400cc, 21,000 km, 原鈑件/原廠保養/新車保固中, dealer 台新汽車 (台南), asking 1,858,000 — a genuinely low-mileage TWO-year-old current-generation car. At 豪華版 list that is 75.5% dealer retail at 2 years. Back-solving one year gives a year-1 dealer retail asking of roughly 2,020,000 (82.1% of list), slightly softer than the 2,050,000 the previous version used. CEILING CHECK: a new 豪華版 transacts at ~2,210,000 before 領牌, so 2,020,000 is ~91% of the new street price — near the credible maximum for a one-year-old car. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private_sale set 11.4% below dealer asking = 1,790,000. The 8-15% band is used near its middle, not its thin end: at one year old the private seller faces the WORST competition of the whole curve, because the buyer's alternative is a brand-new car at ~2,210,000 with a full 4-year warranty, and a private seller with no warranty transfer, no financing and no 認證 must discount hard to close that gap. dealer_tradein set 12.0% below private = 1,575,000. Cross-vehicle check: this puts the gasoline RX350 level with the RX350h at year 1 (both ~79.7% of their own real_cost), which is the expected relationship — at one year the two cars are still trading on discount-off-new, and the gasoline's larger cash discount is already inside its lower real_cost.

PRICE UNCHANGED at 1,560,000 / 1,360,000, but the REASONING BEHIND IT IS CORRECTED and the previous justification was wrong in a way worth recording. Re-verified live on 8891 2026-08-11: the 2023 RX350 頂級版 asking 1,898,000 (dealer 東威, 保固中) carries 4.2萬公里 = 42,000 km, NOT 4,200 km as previously recorded. So it is a NORMAL-mileage 3-year-old (14,000 km/yr, above the Taiwan average), and the previous claim that 'its 4,200 km is BELOW this profile's 21,000 km, so the ratio needs no upward nudge' is exactly backwards — this profile at 21,000 km runs HALF that car's odometer and does earn a premium over its 70.8% ratio. Two further live points bracket it: SUM 汽車網 shows a 2023 RX350, 2400cc, 77,210 km, asking 1,688,000 (dealer 順久車業, 嘉義) — the high-mileage end — and a 2024 RX350, 21,000 km, at 1,858,000, i.e. one year newer at identical mileage. WHY THE NUMBER DID NOT MOVE: the mileage credit is absorbed by a hard trim ceiling. Crediting ~3 points of mileage onto 70.8% and ~1.5 points for base trim would imply a 豪華版 dealer asking near 1,845,000 — only 53,000 below the 頂級版 comparable, a trim that costs 220,000 more new. That is not credible. Capping at the ceiling gives ~1,770,000 dealer retail asking (72.0% of 2,460,000, up from the 1,750,000 basis used before), and the private-sale haircut of 11.9% brings it back to 1,560,000. An abc好車網 2023 RX350 豪華版 at 2,278,000 remains EXCLUDED as a stale or misclassified outlier — it exceeds the 頂級版 asking price, which is not credible for a base trim. dealer_tradein 12.8% below private = 1,360,000. DIRECTIONAL CHECK AGAINST THE RX350h, using a like-for-like pair found this revision: SUM lists a 2023 RX 油電, 2500cc, 4WD, 36,132 km, 白金認證, with Mark Levinson / 電動吸門 / 360環景 / 通風加熱電動座椅 — i.e. RX350h 旗艦版 spec — asking 2,158,000 = 70.8% of its 3,050,000 list. The gasoline 2023 頂級版 at 42,000 km asks the SAME 70.8% of its own list. Since the flagship trim structurally retains a LOWER percentage than a mid trim, an equal percentage from the flagship hybrid means the hybrid is ahead on a like-for-like basis by roughly 1.5-2 points at 3 years. That is the size of gap carried here (69.5% vs the RX350h record's 71.2%).

RE-RESEARCHED AS THE REVIEWER ASKED, AND CONFIRMED UNCHANGED at 1,310,000 / 1,130,000 — but on a much better evidence base than before, and with one of the two denominators it previously used shown to be wrong. EXTRAPOLATED: the 5th-gen RX launched in Taiwan in Nov 2022, so the oldest car on the market in Aug 2026 is under 4 years old and no genuine 5-year data for this generation can exist. DENOMINATOR CORRECTION: the previous version priced the predecessor facelift as 豪華版 2,270,000 / 頂級版 2,390,000 / 旗艦版 2,590,000. The TVBS 2021 Lexus RX spec table was fetched live on 2026-08-11 and gives 300豪華版 2,270,000 / 300頂級版 2,440,000 / 300 F Sport 2,640,000 / 300旗艦版 2,640,000 (all 1998cc). The 頂級版 and 旗艦版 figures previously used were the 2015 pre-facelift numbers applied to facelift cars; every ratio below now uses the verified facelift table. NEW MILEAGE-DISCLOSED 5-YEAR CROSS-SECTION, all fetched live from SUM 汽車網 on 2026-08-11 (2021 RX300, i.e. exactly five years old): 旗艦版 27,277 km asking 1,599,000 = 60.6%; 旗艦版 52,000 km 1,498,000 = 56.7%; 旗艦版 82,540 km 1,498,000 = 56.7%; 旗艦版 69,000 km 1,428,000 = 54.1%; 豪華版 151,627 km 1,090,000 = 48.0%; unspecified trim 100,218 km 1,199,000. Six-year support: 8891 2020 RX300 豪華版 22,000 km 1,238,000 = 54.5% (弘達國際泰山旗艦店, explicitly 「原鈑件、低里程認證車」 — certified, so its ratio carries a certification premium and is NOT the non-certified rate); SUM 2020 頂級天窗版 100,000 km 1,198,000 = 49.1%; SUM 2020 F-Sport 101,000 km 1,328,000 = 50.3%. Four-year support: SUM 2022 頂級版 39,192 km 1,599,000 = 65.5%. BUILD: the 27,277 km five-year 旗艦版 at 60.6% is the closest mileage match to this profile (it runs 5,455 km/yr, marginally below this owner's 7,000). The five-year 旗艦版 set implies a mileage gradient of about 1.5 points of list per 10,000 km, so this profile's 35,000 km costs ~1.2 points; base trim is credited ~1.5 points the other way; and ~1.5 points are taken off for the gasoline RX350's specific weakness in Taiwan (it is the slow seller of a hybrid-led range and is cleared with 250,000-310,000 cash off, so used buyers benchmark it against a ~2,210,000 street price rather than the 2,460,000 list). Net ~59.5%, i.e. ~1,465,000 dealer retail asking — within rounding of the 1,476,000 the previous version reached by a cruder route, which is why the price does not move. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private_sale 10.6% below dealer asking = 1,310,000; dealer_tradein 13.7% below private = 1,130,000. Confidence stays low: the ratio is still transferred from a different generation and a different engine (2.0T vs 2.4T).

CORRECTED DOWNWARD (was 1,100,000 / 930,000). The previous version took a 7-year high-mileage floor of ~42% and added a NINE-point low-mileage premium to reach ~51%. The new mileage-disclosed cross-section shows that premium is roughly double what the market actually pays. Measured gradient at six years: 2020 RX300 豪華版 22,000 km 認證 at 54.5% versus 2020 頂級天窗版 100,000 km at 49.1% and 2020 F-Sport 101,000 km at 50.3% — about 5 points of list for 78,000 km, i.e. ~0.7 points per 10,000 km, and part of even that is the certification premium rather than mileage. Applying the real gradient instead of the assumed one: take the six-year ~100,000 km level (~49.7%), credit this profile's 49,000 km (+3.6 points), subtract one year of age (~4.5 points), and subtract the same ~1.5 points for the gasoline model's discount-driven drag, giving ~47.3%. A second route agrees: the seven-to-eight year floor points — 8891 2019 RX300 F Sport 119,000 km asking 1,088,000 (元禾國際, 新北市), SUM 2018 旗艦版 119,000 km 1,038,000 = 40.1% of 2,590,000, SUM 2018 RX300 111,407 km 1,098,000 — sit at 40-46%, and adding ~4-5 points of mileage credit for a 49,000 km car lands in the same high-40s band. ~48% of 2,460,000 = ~1,180,000 dealer retail asking. Sanity check in absolute money: that is 90,000-140,000 above what real 111,000-119,000 km cars of the same age are asked for, for a car one generation newer with less than half their odometer — a credible spread, whereas the previous 1,255,000 was not. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private_sale 11.9% below dealer asking = 1,040,000; dealer_tradein 14.4% below private = 890,000. The private/trade-in spread widens with age because dealers hold older stock longer. NOTE ON CURVE SHAPE: this leg is deliberately the steepest per year of the whole curve (~6.0 points of real_cost per year versus ~5.6 for years 3-5 and ~4.4 for years 7-10). That is not smoothing — it is the warranty cliff. Lexus TW cover is 4 years / 120,000 km plus a free 5th year earned by punctual servicing, so cover lapses exactly at the start of this window, and Taiwan buyers reprice a Lexus the moment it is out of warranty. Confidence low: cross-generation transfer, pre-facelift comparables whose list prices could not be verified, and thin 7-year 豪華版 data.

CORRECTED DOWNWARD (was 900,000 / 750,000). This is the point the reviewer flagged, and re-research says the reviewer is right: the previous figure made the gasoline RX350 cross ABOVE the RX350h at ten years, which the evidence does not support. THE ANCHOR THAT SETTLES IT, found this revision and fetched live from SUM 汽車網 on 2026-08-11: a 2016 Lexus RX200t, 2000cc, 76,792 km, dealer 上藝汽車 (新北市), described as 全場認證五大保證 / 僅跑7萬多 / 原廠保養, asking 838,000. That is the single best-matched ten-year comparable in the entire dataset — 76,792 km against this profile's 70,000 km is essentially the same odometer, so NO mileage premium is owed on top of it, which is precisely the mistake made twice before at this checkpoint. Against the RX200t 豪華版 list it is ~38% of original, and that 38% is a CERTIFIED, dealer-warranted, dealer-retail ask. Supporting cluster, all live: SUM 2016 RX200t 136,914 km 798,000; SUM 2017 RX 94,465 km 828,000 (note the 9-year and 10-year points are essentially flat, which is the real shape of the tail); abc好車網 2016 旗艦版 ~898,000 and 880,000, 2016 頂級版 788,000, 2015 頂級版 1,020,000 and 960,000. Upper-bound outliers explicitly EXCLUDED from the centre: abc好車網 2016 RX200t 旗艦版 at 1,398,000 (元禾國際車業) — re-fetched this revision and it publishes NO mileage at all, so the previous record's '~70,000 km' description of it was unsupported and has been withdrawn; and abc好車網 2015 RX200t 豪華版 at 1,458,000, which is a LEXUS CPO 台中營業所 car carrying a factory-backed certification. Both are aspirational asks that the 838,000 certified car with disclosed mileage contradicts directly. BUILD: strip ~3 points of certification premium off the 38% matched anchor to get the non-certified rate (~35%), then take ~1.5 points off for the gasoline model's discount-driven drag, giving ~34.5% of 2,460,000 = ~850,000 dealer retail asking. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private_sale 12.9% below dealer asking = 740,000; dealer_tradein 16.9% below private = 615,000 — the widest spreads on the curve, because a ten-year-old car ties up a dealer's floor for months. CHAIN CHECK: 740,000 private now sits just BELOW the 788,000-898,000 real dealer asks of same-age predecessors and well below the 838,000 certified car, so 車商售價 > 自售價 holds. The previous 900,000 private-sale figure exceeded the dealer retail asks of real same-age RX 頂級版 and 旗艦版 cars, which is the inversion the reviewer detected. WHY THE GASOLINE SITS BELOW THE HYBRID HERE — the directional answer the reviewer asked for. Three forces push the RX350 down relative to the RX350h and two push back, and the net is small but consistently negative. Down: (1) demand mix — the Taiwan RX range is hybrid-led, the pure-gasoline 350 is the slow seller that dealers clear with 250,000-310,000 cash off, and a used RX350 therefore always competes against a deeply discounted new one; (2) powertrain reputation at 8-10 years — the T24A-FTS is a turbocharged direct-injection four with a turbocharger, high-pressure fuel pump and carbon-fouling exposure, and Taiwan's used buyers discount turbos hard past eight years, whereas the 350h's Atkinson 2.5 plus planetary eCVT has no turbo and no clutch packs and Toyota/Lexus HEV durability is a selling point locally by year ten rather than a worry; (3) running cost weighs more on a buyer spending 740,000 than on one spending 2,245,000, and the hybrid's ~16-17 km/L against ~11-12 km/L is worth real money to that buyer. Back up: (a) the RX350's 2393cc keeps it in the 1,801-2,400cc 牌照稅 bracket at ~11,230/yr while the RX350h's 2487cc falls into the 2,401-3,000cc bracket at ~15,210/yr, so the gasoline car is roughly 4,000-5,000/yr cheaper to run on tax alone; (b) this 豪華版 is AWD where the RX350h 豪華版 is FWD; (c) the hybrid pack is outside its 8yr/160,000 km warranty by year ten and Taiwan buyers still take something off for that. Those counterweights are why the answer is 'slightly below', at ~3 points of retention, and not the 6-8 points a pure reliability narrative would produce. Confidence low: cross-generation ratio transfer, unverifiable 2015/2016 RX200t list prices (the U-CAR launch article returns HTTP 403 and could not be confirmed this revision either), and a wide listing spread.

maintenance.plan_notes: Unchanged in this revision — the reviewer's objection was confined to the resale curve and no new maintenance evidence was found. NO free scheduled-maintenance program. Lexus Taiwan gives only the 滿月保養 (free 1-month / 24-point inspection after registration) plus a free 25-point premium 健檢 at each visit — every routine service is owner-paid parts and labour from day one, so no free-programme credit is taken. The official 保養計劃 was VERIFIED on lexus.com.tw: 1個月 (24-point); 6個月/10,000km (16-point, oil + filter, battery test); 12個月/20,000km (29-point, air filter, plugs); 24個月/40,000km (34-point, brake fluid, transmission fluid check); 48個月/80,000km (37-point, coolant + fuel filter). AT 7,000 KM/YEAR THIS IS PURELY TIME-DRIVEN — the owner hits every interval on the calendar and never on the odometer, so it is TWO dealer visits per year for the whole ten years, ~3,500 km apart. That is the single biggest cost driver here and it is why low mileage does not cut the servicing bill anywhere near proportionally. Warranty was also VERIFIED on lexus.com.tw: 4 years / 120,000 km, with a FREE extension to the 5th year / 140,000 km granted only if every 6-month service is kept punctual (miss one and eligibility is forfeited); 12V battery 3 years (free replacement in years 0-2, 50% in years 2-3), tyres 3 years pro-rata on remaining tread, spark plugs to their first scheduled change. This profile trivially satisfies the km side, so years 1-5 carry essentially zero unscheduled repair cost. Per-visit cost is anchored on real owner receipts from a VERIFIED PTT 車板 thread: a routine 半年定保 quoted at 10,600 of which only ~4,000 is mandatory (the ~6,000 of 建議項目 are routinely declined), plus owners reporting 6萬km service at 3,800 and 7萬公里 原廠保養 at 4,000+. HONESTY FLAG: the same verified thread also contains owners reporting 17,000 for one visit and 'never less than 20,000 per visit'. The decline-the-add-ons model is internally consistent and is what a cost-conscious owner actually does, but it sits at the cheap end of the observed distribution. Out-of-warranty allowances from year 7 are kept moderate: this is a Toyota T24A-FTS turbo four in a Lexus, with no air suspension and no chronic coil-pack or water-pump pattern to provision for, so German-car risk loading does not apply. TYRE TIMING: 235/60R19 on a ~2.1-tonne SUV at 7,000 km/yr will time out on rubber age long before it wears out. The first set has covered only ~35,000 km at year 5 with plenty of tread and is barely at the early edge of the age window, so it is replaced at ~year 6 (booked in the 5-7 checkpoint), which is the normal age-out call. Consequence: the set fitted at year 6 is only 4 years old with ~28,000 km at the 10-year mark and is NOT yet due, so no second set is booked in the 7-10 window — it would fall around year 12, outside this horizon. Total ten-year maintenance spend ~248,000. NOTE ON THE HYBRID COMPARISON: this car's ten-year maintenance total sits ~37,000 BELOW the RX350h record's, which is the correct direction — the hybrid provisions for a high-voltage pack that is out of warranty by year ten. That maintenance advantage for the gasoline car is real, and it is accounted for here rather than being smuggled into the resale curve, which is part of why the resale curve is allowed to sit slightly below the hybrid's.

Build: four scheduled visits (~4,000 + ~9,000 brake fluid at 72 months + ~4,000 + ~7,000 = 24,000) + first tyre set 30,000 + alignment 2,000 + 12V battery 8,000 + front pads and discs 12,000 + out-of-warranty allowance 8,000 = 84,000. checkpoints.source: Covers 7-10 years. Unchanged in this revision. Scheduled backbone from the verified Lexus TW 保養計劃 (the 48-month cycle repeats at 96 months). Build: six visits totalling ~35,000 including the 96-month major at ~13,000, plus plugs 8,000 + second battery 8,000 + rear brakes 15,000 + ageing allowance 35,000 = 101,000. Consumable and ageing items are estimates for a 10-year-old low-mileage RX in Taiwan, not sourced receipts. Deliberately less aggressive than a German equivalent would need: Lexus RX reliability is strong and verified PTT owners consistently report cheap high-mileage dealer servicing. Note the tension with the resale curve, stated openly: this record argues the T24A-FTS turbo is discounted by 10-year used buyers relative to the hybrid, yet books no turbo-specific failure here. That is deliberate — a turbocharger failure is a tail risk that a used buyer prices in as a discount long before it becomes an expected cost, and the ageing allowance is the single largest uncertainty in the record either way, hence low confidence.
